title: Sirtuin 1 inhibition: a promising avenue to suppress cancer progression through small inhibitors design.
authors: Ullah, Atta; Waqas, Muhammad; Halim, Sobia Ahsan; Daud, Muhammad; Jan, Afnan; Khan, Ajmal; Al-Harrasi, Ahmed
one_liner_zh: 该文研究SIRT1小分子抑制剂与p53互作，属于蛋白-蛋白体系，无DNA互作，仅用分子对接和MD，与本课题TF-DNA无关。
abstract: SIRT1 is a protein associated with vital cell functions such as gene regulation, metabolism, ageing, and cellular energy restoration. Its association with the tumor suppressor protein p53 is essential for controlling the growth of cells, apoptosis, and response to DNA damage. By raising p53 acetylation, encouraging apoptosis, and reducing cell proliferation, inhibiting SIRT1's catalytic domain, which interacts with p53, shows potential as a cancer treatment. The aim of the study is to find compounds that could inhibit SIRT1 and thus lower the proliferation of cancer cells. Employing molecular docking techniques, a virtual screening of  approximately 900 compounds (isolated from medicinal plants and derivatives) gave us 13 active compounds with good binding affinity. Additional evaluation of pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties led to the selection of eight compounds with desirable properties. Docking analysis confirmed stable interactions between the final eight compounds (C1-C8) and the SIRT1 catalytic domain. Molecular dynamics simulations show overall stability and moderate changes in protein structure upon compound binding. The compactness of the protein indicated the protein's tight packing upon the inhibitors binding. Binding free energy calculations revealed that compounds C2 (-49.96 +/- 0.073 kcal/mol and C1 (-44.79 +/- 0.077 kcal/mol) exhibited the highest energy, indicating strong binding affinity to the SIRT1 catalytic domain. These compounds, along with C8, C5, C6, C3, C4 and C7, showed promising potential as SIRT1 inhibitors. Based on their ability to reduce SIRT1 activity and increase apoptosis, the eight chemicals discovered in this work may be useful in treating cancer.Communicated by Ramaswamy H. Sarma.
abstract_zh: SIRT1是一种与基因调控、代谢、衰老及细胞能量恢复等关键细胞功能相关的蛋白质。其与肿瘤抑制蛋白p53的关联对于控制细胞生长、凋亡及DNA损伤应答至关重要。通过提高p53乙酰化、促进凋亡及减少细胞增殖，抑制SIRT1的催化结构域（该结构域与p53相互作用）显示出作为癌症治疗的潜力。本研究旨在寻找能够抑制SIRT1从而降低癌细胞增殖的化合物。采用分子对接 (molecular docking) 技术，对约900种化合物（分离自药用植物及其衍生物）进行虚拟筛选，得到13种具有良好结合亲和力的活性化合物。进一步评估药代动力学和药效学特性后，筛选出8种具有理想性质的化合物。对接分析确认了最终8种化合物（C1-C8）与SIRT1催化结构域之间的稳定相互作用。分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟显示，化合物结合后蛋白质结构整体稳定且发生适度变化。蛋白质的紧凑性表明抑制剂结合后蛋白质紧密包裹。结合自由能计算显示，化合物C2（-49.96 +/- 0.073 kcal/mol）和C1（-44.79 +/- 0.077 kcal/mol）表现出最高能量，表明其与SIRT1催化结构域具有强结合亲和力。这些化合物连同C8、C5、C6、C3、C4和C7，显示出作为SIRT1抑制剂的良好潜力。基于其降低SIRT1活性并增加凋亡的能力，本工作中发现的这8种化学物质可能有助于癌症治疗。由Ramaswamy H. Sarma通讯。
